Issues.Title: Fix exception parameter names and messages
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7943.

Pass `(paramName, value, msg)` when constructing exceptions in both non-formatting `ExceptParamValue` overloads.
Previously, the error message became `ParamName` and the parameter name became the message.
The regression checks the name, value, and message with and without an exception context; all three `TestContracts` cases pass on net10.0 and net11.0.

The host lacks Clang/native libraries, so the root build could not complete.
These managed tests use an external native-copy override and the test framework's existing `SKIP_MKL` switch; neither changes the submitted code.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Fix exception parameter names and messages" (#7944)

Issues.Title: ExceptParamValue swaps the exception parameter name and message
Issues.Body:
The two non-formatting `Contracts.ExceptParamValue<T>` overloads pass `(msg, value, paramName)` to `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`, whose constructor expects `(paramName, actualValue, message)`.

For example, `Contracts.ExceptParamValue(-7, "count", "Count must be positive.")` sets `ParamName` to `"Count must be positive."` and uses `"count"` as the message.
The overload with an `IExceptionContext` has the same behavior.
Both formatting overloads already use the correct order.

Confirmed on main at a3d5f26654803cdd3851a5cacda97e483d890373.
A two-case regression fails on the original code and passes with the arguments corrected.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "ExceptParamValue swaps the exception parameter name and message" (#7943)

Issues.Title: Preserve progress subchannel identity and nesting level
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7941.

Creating multiple progress channels at the same depth currently reuses the depth as their dictionary ID and stores the unique ID as the nesting level.
Pass `(root, newId, level)` to `SubChannel` so sibling channels remain independent and progress is ordered by actual nesting depth.

The regression covers sibling and nested channels, aggregated metric values, and disposal without removing another channel's progress.
It fails at the duplicate-ID assertion before the fix and passes on both net10.0 and net11.0 afterward.

The root build could not complete because this Linux host lacks Clang/native libraries.
Focused managed tests were built with an external target that skips native copies and enables the test framework's existing `SKIP_MKL` switch; the override is outside the repository and is not included in this PR.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Preserve progress subchannel identity and nesting level" (#7942)

Issues.Title: Progress subchannel constructor receives the ID and nesting level in reverse order
Issues.Body:
On current main `a3d5f26654803cdd3851a5cacda97e483d890373`, `ProgressChannel.StartProgressChannel(int level)` calls `new SubChannel(this, level, newId)`, while the constructor takes `(root, id, level)`.

Creating a second root child therefore reuses ID 1 and fails the duplicate-channel assertion in Debug.
The unique channel ID is also used as its nesting level, although progress entries are ordered by nesting level.

I would like to correct the argument order and add a regression covering sibling channels, a nested child, progress aggregation and independent disposal.
The regression fails at the duplicate-channel assertion before the fix and passes on .NET 10 and .NET 11 afterward.

The root build is blocked on this Linux host by missing Clang/native libraries.
The focused managed regression was built and executed using an external target that skips native-library copies and enables the test framework's existing `SKIP_MKL` initialization switch; neither setting is part of the proposed repository change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Progress subchannel constructor receives the ID and nesting level in reverse order" (#7941)

Issues.Title: Make BertTokenizer strip accents in globalization-invariant mode
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7728

`BertOptions.RemoveNonSpacingMarks` strips accents with `string.Normalize(NormalizationForm.FormD)`. In globalization-invariant mode `string.Normalize` returns its input unchanged, so the accents stay and, with uncased vocabularies, words like "café" become `[UNK]`. Invariant mode is common: the Native AOT templates and the default Alpine and chiseled container images turn it on.

## Changes

- When `string.Normalize` doesn't work, `BertNormalizer` removes the accents using a table instead. For each character whose canonical decomposition contains non-spacing marks, the table holds the character without them (é → e). Nothing changes when ICU or NLS is available.
- There's no public API to detect invariant mode yet (dotnet/runtime#81429), so it checks whether `Normalize` decomposes "é".
- The table (991 characters, about 8 KB) is generated from the Unicode Character Database 18.0.0 by a small tool in `tools-local/GenerateNonSpacingMarkTable`. As with the Unicode tables in dotnet/runtime, the tool isn't part of the build, and its Readme explains how to update the table.
- I added the Unicode license to THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.TXT, since the table comes from Unicode data.

Accent stripping shouldn't depend on the environment, and in Hugging Face it doesn't: its Python BERT tokenizer uses Python's built-in `unicodedata`, and its Rust tokenizers use the `unicode-normalization` crate. Both carry their own Unicode data, so the same text gives the same tokens on every machine.

I didn't go with the issue's other option, throwing from `BertTokenizer.Create` in invariant mode. It would break apps that work today because their text has no accents, and it still wouldn't give the right tokens.

## Tests

Two new tests run `BertTokenizer` in a separate process with invariant mode on (RemoteExecutor). One repeats the accent cases of `TestWithAccentMarks`; the other checks that every character the runtime can decompose gives the same result as with ICU. Both fail without the fix. They only run on .NET, as .NET Framework has no invariant mode.

## Not in this PR

The tokenizer.json `StripAccents` and `NFC`/`NFD`/`NFKC`/`NFKD` normalizer steps have the same problem in invariant mode. They're left for a separate change.

<details>
<summary>Checking the table with Python</summary>

This prints the table's mapping using Python's own Unicode data. Python 3.11 has Unicode 14, so its output doesn't include the table's 3 newer characters (U+105C9, U+105E4 and U+11385).

```python
import unicodedata as ud

for cp in range(0x110000):
    c = chr(cp)
    if ud.category(c) in ('Mn', 'Cs'):
        continue
    d = ud.normalize('NFD', c)
    if any(ud.category(x) == 'Mn' for x in d):
        r = ud.normalize('NFC', ''.join(x for x in d if ud.category(x) != 'Mn'))
        if r != c:
            print(f'U+{cp:04X} -> {" ".join(f"U+{ord(x):04X}" for x in r)}')
```

</details>

Issues.Title: [macOS x64] SymSgdNative segfaults in OpenMP barrier with duplicate runtime images
Issues.Body:
## Summary

A macOS x64 Helix run of `Microsoft.ML.Tests` segfaulted while `NonDefaultColNamesBinaryClassificationOnnxConversionTest` was training SymSGD. The captured native stack enters SymSGD's OpenMP parallel region and crosses from `libomp.dylib` into `libiomp5.dylib`'s `__kmp_suspend_64`. This is consistent with the Helix payload loading two images of the same OpenMP library under different names. The stack is strong evidence of the interaction, but the precise dyld symbol-binding mechanism and a product-level reproducer still need confirmation.

## Reproducible CI evidence

- Repository: dotnet/machinelearning
- Azure Pipelines build: [MachineLearning-CI build 1690596 (20261119.12)](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1690596)
- Source: 2a5763c64e0a5ee55b58714fb17fcd09cadcb40f
- Leg/queue: `MacOS_x64 Debug_Build` / `osx.15.amd64.open`
- OS: macOS 15.7
- [Helix console log](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-machinelearning-refs-pull-7931-merge-1cb483bbe67149679d/Microsoft.ML.Tests/1/console.970b4ba8.log?helixlogtype=result)
- [Crash report JSON](https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-machinelearning-refs-pull-7931-merge-1cb483bbe67149679d/Microsoft.ML.Tests/1/coredump.65758.1795114549.dmp.crashreport.json?helixlogtype=result)

The test was identified from the crash report's thread stacks, not just from the last `Starting test:` line in the console (xUnit runs tests concurrently).

## Crash evidence

The crash report marks native thread `0xc1091` as crashing. Its relevant frames are:

```
libiomp5.dylib!__kmp_suspend_64<false, true>
libomp.dylib!kmp_flag_64<false, true>::wait
libomp.dylib!__kmp_hyper_barrier_release
libomp.dylib!__kmp_fork_barrier
libomp.dylib!__kmp_launch_thread
libomp.dylib!__kmp_launch_worker
```

Another captured thread shows the application path entering this OpenMP region:

```
libiomp5.dylib!__kmp_suspend_64<false, true>
libomp.dylib!kmp_flag_64<false, true>::wait
libomp.dylib!__kmp_hyper_barrier_gather
libomp.dylib!__kmp_join_barrier
libomp.dylib!__kmpc_fork_call
libSymSgdNative.dylib!InitializeState
libSymSgdNative.dylib!LearnAll
SymbolicSgdLogisticRegressionBinaryTrainer.TrainCore
OnnxConversionTest.TestPipeline
Microsoft.ML.Tests.OnnxConversionTest.NonDefaultColNamesBinaryClassificationOnnxConversionTest
```

The dump lists the two libraries as separate loaded images at bases `0x1a9c38000` (`libiomp5.dylib`) and `0x1abe17000` (`libomp.dylib`).

## Relevant runtime setup

At the source commit above:

- [`eng/helix.proj`](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/2a5763c64e0a5ee55b58714fb17fcd09cadcb40f/eng/helix.proj#L112-L162) sets `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE`, copies Homebrew's `libomp.dylib` into the test payload, and on macOS x64 copies that file again as `libiomp5.dylib`.
- [`SymSgdNative/CMakeLists.txt`](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/2a5763c64e0a5ee55b58714fb17fcd09cadcb40f/src/Native/SymSgdNative/CMakeLists.txt#L9-L45) links SymSGD against Homebrew's `libomp` on macOS.
- The loaded `libiomp5.dylib` name is needed by MKL's `libMklImports.dylib`.

This makes the duplicate-runtime setup a plausible cause, but it does not by itself prove why dyld bound this particular call across the two images.

## Requested investigation

1. Reproduce or otherwise confirm the crash and determine whether loading the same OpenMP binary under both `libomp.dylib` and `libiomp5.dylib` causes the cross-image call/state mismatch.
2. Adjust the macOS x64 Helix native-library setup so MKL, SymSGD, and other native dependencies use a compatible single OpenMP runtime, without changing Linux's separate fix in #7927.
3. Consider improving [`eng/testing/runTests.sh`](https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/2a5763c64e0a5ee55b58714fb17fcd09cadcb40f/eng/testing/runTests.sh#L1-L57): when a test process exits due to a native crash, print the crashing thread's native frames from the generated crash-report JSON to the console. This would make future failures easier to identify and provide a stable Build Analysis signature even when Helix artifacts are no longer available.

Related context: #7061, #7734, and #5569. #7927 addresses a Linux x64 OpenMP-linking issue and does not change macOS.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue draft was prepared with GitHub Copilot; the root-cause mechanism above is a hypothesis to verify.

Issues.Title: Use MKL's libiomp5 for SymSgdNative OpenMP on Linux x64
Issues.Body:
Fixes #6972. Related to #7925.

On linux-x64, `libSymSgdNative.so` needed two OpenMP runtimes: `libiomp5.so` (through `libMklImports.so`) and `libomp.so.5`. Azure Linux doesn't ship `libomp.so.5`, so SymSGD couldn't load there.

This change links SymSgdNative against a build-only `libiomp5.so` stub. Its OpenMP calls then resolve from the same `libiomp5.so` that MKL already loads. The stub isn't installed or packaged. Other platforms are unchanged.

Docs now list how to get `libiomp5.so` on Debian/Ubuntu and Azure Linux.

Issues.Title: Move PR cross-builds to Azure Linux 4
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Move the x64, arm and arm64 PR/CI cross-builds to Azure Linux 4 .NET 11 images.
- Use the cross toolchain for x64 when a target rootfs is supplied, and find the restored MKL library outside the sysroot.
- Update the build documentation for the new images and rootfs paths.

The CentOS x64 CI job remains for now because it matches the official shipping build. This PR does not change the official pipeline or the existing Helix images. Those migrations and the OpenMP compatibility decision are tracked in dotnet/machinelearning#7925.

The arm job requires dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker#1829 to be merged and its image published before it can pass.

## Validation

- [x] x64 native Debug build in `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-amd64`
- [x] Full x64 Debug PR build in `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-amd64`
- [x] arm64 native Debug build in `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-arm64`
- [x] arm native Debug build with the OpenMP sysroot fix from dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker#1829
- [x] Load the cross-built x64 `libSymSgdNative.so` on Ubuntu 24.04 with `libomp5` and `libomp-dev`
- [x] Two focused x64 SymSGD tests passed on Ubuntu 24.04 with the direct VSTest runner (no skips). A separate `dotnet vstest` invocation reported success but did not exit and was stopped.
- [x] Validate shell and pipeline YAML syntax
- [ ] PR/CI Helix runs against the published fixed arm image

The cross-built x64 library requires `libomp.so.5`. On Azure Linux 4, installing `libomp` alone does not provide that name or the MKL dependency `libiomp5.so`; merely adding compatibility names allowed the library to load, but that is not an end-to-end ABI or test validation. The shipping compatibility contract and Azure Linux Helix setup remain open.


### Y2038 (linux-arm)

Native builds now define `_TIME_BITS=64` and `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64`, matching dotnet/runtime and .NET 9+ Arm32 Y2038 support (dotnet/runtime#101944, dotnet/iot#2307). This only affects 32-bit glibc targets. A local Release arm build shows a maximum requirement of `GLIBC_2.32`, which is within .NET 11's Arm32 floor of glibc 2.35. The ML.NET native assets import no 32-bit `time_t` or file-offset glibc APIs.

Issues.Title: Move Linux builds off stale CentOS Stream 8 and Ubuntu 22.04 images to Azure Linux 4 cross images
Issues.Body:
## Summary

ML.NET's Linux build and test infrastructure depends on stale or retiring container images. Most importantly, the **official** Linux x64 native package assets are built in `centos-stream8-mlnet`, an image whose Dockerfile was deleted from dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker more than two years ago.

We expect to stop building the `net8.0` cross images in the first half of 2027. If ML.NET still uses them, its official and PR/CI arm and arm64 builds will soon depend on frozen, increasingly stale images, much like the current CentOS Stream 8 image. Stopping image builds does not by itself mean the published images will immediately disappear or their Dockerfiles will be deleted.

We intend to move all Linux native builds to the Azure Linux 4 `net11.0` cross-build images, matching [the approach dotnet/runtime took when it moved off CentOS 7](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/83428).

## Current state

| Pipeline | Target | Image | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Official (`build/vsts-ci.yml`) | linux-x64 | `centos-stream8-mlnet` | **Stale.** Last published 2024-05-29; Dockerfile deleted in dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker#1086 (2024-06-05). CentOS Stream 8 reached end of life on 2024-05-31. |
| Official | linux-arm, linux-arm64 | `azurelinux-3.0-net8.0-cross-arm` / `-arm64` | .NET 8-era cross images (Ubuntu 16.04 target rootfs); expected to stop being built in the first half of 2027 |
| PR/CI (`.vsts-dotnet-ci.yml`) | x64 (`Centos_x64`) | `centos-stream8-mlnet` | Same stale image |
| PR/CI | x64 (`Ubuntu_x64`) | `ubuntu-22.04-mlnet` | Ubuntu 22.04 images are being retired |
| PR/CI | arm, arm64 | `azurelinux-3.0-net8.0-cross-arm` / `-arm64` | Same .NET 8-era cross images |
| Helix (x64) | — | `centos-stream9-mlnet-helix`, `ubuntu-22.04-mlnet-helix` | ML.NET-specific images; only add OpenMP |
| Nightly (`build/.night-build.yml`) | — | `ubuntu-22.04-mlnet` | Pipeline definition is currently disabled |

The x64 official build is a non-cross build in an end-of-life distro container: it produces shipping binaries from a toolchain and package set that no longer receives updates, and the image cannot be rebuilt.

## Plan

1. **PR/CI pipeline** (first PR)
   - Build x64, arm, and arm64 with:
     - `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-amd64` (Ubuntu 18.04 target rootfs)
     - `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-arm64` (Ubuntu 18.04 target rootfs)
     - `azurelinux-4.0-net11.0-cross-arm` (Ubuntu 22.04 target rootfs)
   - Replace `Ubuntu_x64` with an x64 cross-build job. Keep `Centos_x64` temporarily for side-by-side comparison with the shipping x64 build.
   - Define `_TIME_BITS=64` and `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64` for Unix native builds, matching dotnet/runtime (Y2038 for linux-arm).
   - Update `src/Native/build.sh` so it uses `eng/common/cross/toolchain.cmake` whenever `ROOTFS_DIR` is set, not only for arm/arm64.
   - The shared rootfs script already installs `libomp5` and `libomp-dev` for ML.NET in these target rootfs images.
2. **x64 Helix tests**
   - Decide how x64 tests get the OpenMP runtime: add it to a Helix image in dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker, or install it at test time as the ARM Helix queues already do.
   - Run Helix tests on Azure Linux, with Ubuntu as secondary coverage if needed.
3. **Official build**
   - Move `Linux_x64`, `Linux_arm`, and `Linux_arm64` to the same Azure Linux 4 cross images.
   - Compare the resulting binaries' glibc and OpenMP requirements against current shipping binaries before merging.
4. **Cleanup**
   - Remove remaining references to `centos-stream8-mlnet`, `ubuntu-22.04-mlnet`, and the ML.NET-specific Helix images.
   - Retire those images in dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker once nothing consumes them.

## Compatibility notes

ML.NET packages target `netstandard2.0`. They are consumed on .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11, so the relevant floor is the oldest supported .NET consumer, not only .NET 11.

| .NET | glibc floor (x64, arm64) | glibc floor (arm32) |
|---|---|---|
| 8.0 | 2.23 (Ubuntu 16.04) | 2.23 |
| 9.0 | 2.23 | 2.35 (Y2038) |
| 10.0 | 2.27 (Ubuntu 18.04) | 2.35 |
| 11.0 | 2.27 | 2.35 |

The target sysroot, not the build host, determines `DT_NEEDED` names and symbol versions. Building on an Azure Linux host against an Ubuntu sysroot produces Ubuntu-flavored dependencies.

### Measured results

| Asset | Shipped 6.0.0 | New cross-build |
|---|---|---|
| SymSGD x64 | GLIBC_2.27, `libomp.so` | GLIBC_2.27 (Debug), `libomp.so.5` |
| SymSGD arm64 | GLIBC_2.17, `libomp.so.5` | GLIBC_2.27 (Debug), `libomp.so.5` |
| SymSGD arm | GLIBC_2.4, GLIBCXX_3.4.21, `libomp.so.5` | GLIBC_2.27, GLIBCXX_3.4.29 (Release), `libomp.so.5` |
| Lda arm | GLIBC_2.4, GLIBCXX_3.4.21 | GLIBC_2.32, GLIBCXX_3.4.30 (Release) |
| MatrixFactorization arm | not yet compared | GLIBC_2.32, GLIBCXX_3.4.30 (Release) |
| Lda arm64 | GLIBC_2.17 | not yet measured (Release) |

- The SymSGD increase comes from `expf`, `log2f`, and `powf`. glibc 2.27 introduced new symbol versions for them, so linking against glibc 2.27 or later selects `GLIBC_2.27`. Older sysroots select the architecture's base version (2.17 for arm64, 2.4 for arm). x64 did not change because CentOS Stream 8 (glibc 2.28) already selected the 2.27 versions.
- The arm32 increases (GLIBC_2.32, GLIBCXX_3.4.30 / GCC 12 libstdc++) come from the Ubuntu 22.04 sysroot. These are within .NET 9+'s Y2038 arm32 baseline (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12).
- **Y2038 (unverified):** The proposed build defines `_TIME_BITS=64` and `_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64`. A limited import scan found no obvious direct 32-bit time or file-offset glibc APIs in the three newly built arm32 native libraries. That alone does not establish Y2038 compatibility or prove exported and transitive-library ABIs are unchanged. See dotnet/runtime#101944 and dotnet/iot#2307.
- **Arm32 sysroot nuance:** We have not identified an ML.NET-specific Y2038 issue that independently requires an Ubuntu 22.04 sysroot, although transitive dependencies and behavior beyond 2038 remain unverified. .NET 10's supported arm32 baseline already requires glibc 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04), so choosing that sysroot does not raise the glibc floor for supported .NET 10 consumers, provided the actual artifacts stay within that floor. Other dependencies, including libstdc++, still need separate compatibility checks.
- **Modern arm32 smoke test:** On emulated Debian 13 (glibc 2.41) with `libomp5` installed, the shipped 6.0.0 arm32 SymSGD and Lda libraries loaded, and a small two-thread SymSGD training call succeeded. This did not test a .NET application, all native assets, or dates beyond 2038.
- **Native time-ABI review:** The arm32 native assets are SymSGD, Lda, and MatrixFactorization. A source and dynamic-import scan found no direct `time_t`/time API boundary in SymSGD or MatrixFactorization. Lda uses `std::chrono::steady_clock` and `high_resolution_clock`; its `get_time()` converts a chrono duration to `double`, and no direct `time_t` API call was found. This is narrower than the .NET/OpenSSL mismatch in dotnet/runtime#101444, but it is not a full audit of transitive libraries or a proof of Y2038 behavior. On emulated Debian 13, the shipped SymSGD and Lda loaded and a two-thread SymSGD training smoke test passed; the proposed MatrixFactorization library also loaded. These checks do not test a full .NET app or dates beyond 2038.

## Proposal: target `net10.0` alongside `netstandard2.0`

Consider updating ML.NET packages that currently target only `netstandard2.0` to multi-target `netstandard2.0;net10.0`, in line with the .NET package-servicing direction proposed in dotnet/core#10717. The PR identifies ML.NET as a latest-version-serviced package and clarifies that .NET Standard compatibility does not imply support on every runtime that can consume it; packages should support in-support .NET versions and operating systems.

This proposal would make `net10.0` the explicit asset for current .NET consumers and give ML.NET a place for .NET 10-specific implementation/build choices. It would also establish the relevant current Linux compatibility floors as .NET 10's: glibc 2.27 on x64/arm64 and 2.35 on arm32. The measured proposed builds require `GLIBC_2.27` for x64/arm64 SymSGD (Debug), and up to `GLIBC_2.32` and `GLIBCXX_3.4.30` for the tested arm32 libraries (Release). Complete Release/all-assets validation and check libstdc++ availability separately.

**Important limitation:** retaining `netstandard2.0` means older .NET runtimes can still restore that asset. Multi-targeting does not itself block those applications or guarantee the native binaries remain loadable there. We must explicitly decide whether to retain that compatibility path, document it as unsupported, and/or provide a warning or other signal; confirm actual NuGet asset selection and package native-asset layout before treating this as the resolution to the compatibility concerns below. This is a package policy/support proposal, not yet a decision to drop `netstandard2.0` or change the official build.

Reference: dotnet/core#10717 (https://github.com/dotnet/core/pull/10717).

## Breaking changes

### Known

1. **x64 OpenMP SONAME: `libomp.so` → `libomp.so.5`** (when the official x64 build moves). The shipped x64 SymSGD was built in CentOS (RHEL family) and records `libomp.so`. The Ubuntu sysroot records `libomp.so.5`. Azure Linux 4's `libomp` package provides only `libomp.so`, and a cross-built binary failed to load there without compatibility links. Conversely, Debian-family systems with only `libomp5` gain support. This needs an explicit decision before shipping: keep `libomp.so`, standardize on `libomp.so.5`, link differently, or bundle a runtime.
2. **arm32 floor rises to glibc 2.32 / GCC 12 libstdc++ (GLIBCXX_3.4.30).** This breaks arm32 consumers on .NET 8 on older distros (for example, Debian 10/11, Ubuntu 20.04, Raspberry Pi OS based on Debian 11). This is acceptable given .NET 9+'s arm32 Y2038 baseline. It needs a release note.
3. **arm64 SymSGD floor rises from GLIBC_2.17 to GLIBC_2.27.** This only matters for .NET 8 arm64 consumers on glibc 2.23–2.26 (for example, Ubuntu 16.04). Those are below .NET 10+'s floor. It needs a release note.

### Possible, unproven

- **arm32 Y2038 ABI compatibility.** The old sysroot does not by itself prove that ML.NET fails on modern distros, but an older binary can encounter an ABI mismatch when it exchanges `time_t` or time-bearing structures with a newer system library. Test the shipped and proposed artifacts end-to-end on modern arm32 distros, including relevant dependencies and dates beyond 2038. The .NET 8/OpenSSL issue in dotnet/runtime#101444 is an example of this class of problem, not proof that ML.NET has the same failure.
- **OpenMP ABI across implementations.** `libomp.so` (LLVM, RHEL family/Azure Linux) and `libomp.so.5` (Debian) may be the same LLVM runtime under different names, but this hasn't been verified for all versions. A symlink loader test succeeded; functional and ABI tests haven't been run.
- **Release x64 and arm64.** Only Debug SymSGD was measured for these. Release builds of all packaged assets (Lda, MatrixFactorization, CpuMath, FastTree, MklProxy, and so on) still need `DT_NEEDED`, `GLIBC_*`, and `GLIBCXX_*` checks against the shipped 6.0.0 assets.
- **MKL / `libiomp5.so`.** `libMklImports.so` is restored separately and requires `libiomp5.so`. The sysroot change should not affect it, but its interaction with a different SymSGD OpenMP runtime in the same process hasn't been tested.
- **x64 libstdc++ floor.** The x64 Ubuntu 18.04 sysroot (GCC 7/8 libstdc++) should be at or below CentOS Stream 8's, but this hasn't been measured.
- **Toolchain change.** Shipped x64 was built with Red Hat Clang 17.0.6 (per `.comment`). The Azure Linux 4 cross image uses a newer Clang with a different sysroot, which may change floating-point codegen and therefore numeric test baselines.

## References

- PR/CI change: https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/pull/7926
- arm OpenMP sysroot fix: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker/pull/1829
- .NET Arm32 Y2038: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/101944, https://github.com/dotnet/iot/issues/2307
- .NET 11 supported OS / glibc floors: https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/supported-os.md

- CentOS Stream 8 Dockerfile deletion: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker/pull/1086
- Official build: https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/main/build/vsts-ci.yml
- PR/CI build: https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/main/.vsts-dotnet-ci.yml
- Native build script: https://github.com/dotnet/machinelearning/blob/main/src/Native/build.sh
- Azure Linux 4 x64 cross image: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker/blob/main/src/azurelinux/4.0/net11.0/cross/amd64/Dockerfile
- Rootfs OpenMP packages: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker/blob/main/eng/common/cross/build-rootfs.sh#L122-L124

Issues.Title: Apply SentencePiece charsmap entries that map to an empty string
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7908

`NormalizePrefix` used an empty `Memory<byte>` to mean "no rule matched", and the callers checked `Length == 0` for that. A charsmap entry whose replacement is "" also has length 0, so the original bytes were written instead and the char was encoded as `<unk>`. nmt_nfkc deletes 30 code points this way (U+0001-U+0008, U+000B, U+000E-U+001F, U+007F, U+008F, U+009F).

Change: `NormalizePrefix` now returns the bytes to write as a `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` (the input slice, the replacement char, or the charsmap value, which can be empty). The leading whitespace loop stops on an empty replacement, same as SentencePiece's `p.first != " "` check. This covers both the `.model` path and the `tokenizer.json` Precompiled step, since that one goes through the same normalizer.

Two related changes:
- The existing Unigram test row for `"\u001f"` expected `[▁, <unk>]`, which was the bug. It now expects an empty result, matching SentencePiece and HF.
- Input that normalizes to nothing hit `Debug.Assert(normalized.Length > 0)` in `SentencePieceUnigramModel.Encode`. That already happens on main for whitespace-only input like `"   "` in Debug builds. Release was fine because `NormalizeText` returns an empty span for that case and `Encode` handles size 0. I removed the assert and added a `"   "` row.

Not touched: the tie-breaking difference in #7909.

Tests: 30 code points x (`.model`, `tokenizer.json`) checking that `a{c}b`, `{c}hello`, `hello{c}` and so on encode the same as without the char and never produce `<unk>`, plus a check that tab is still mapped to a space. `Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers.Tests` on net8.0: 511 passed. Release build has no warnings. I couldn't run net48/net9.0 locally.

Issues.Title: Fix ToArrowRecordBatches including arrays from earlier batches
Issues.Body:
Fixes #7799

`ToArrowRecordBatches()` created the `arrays` list once, outside the batching loop, so every batch after the first also got the earlier batches' arrays. With one column split into two batches, batch 1 had one schema field but two arrays, and `FromArrowRecordBatch` on it threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. The list is now created per batch.

The issue also asks that continuing the enumeration can't change a batch that was already yielded. With Apache.Arrow 14.0.2 `RecordBatch` copies the list it gets, so that wasn't happening on main, but with a new list per batch it can't happen either way. The test enumerates all batches first (`ToList()`) and then checks both, so it would catch it.

Added `TestRecordBatchesAcrossMultipleBuffers`: an int column one value past a buffer's capacity, so it exports as two batches. It checks each batch has one array and that the second batch reimports with the right value. It needs a bit over 2 GB, so it's an `[X64Fact]` like the multi-buffer tests in `PrimitiveDataFrameColumnTests`. I'm on an arm64 Mac where `X64Fact` skips, so I ran it locally as a plain `[Fact]`: it fails on main (`Assert.Single() Failure: The collection contained 2 items`) and passes with the fix. The rest of Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests passes (1780 passed, 7 skipped, net8.0). I also ran the repro from the issue before and after, and the output now matches the expected output there.

This doesn't touch #7800 or #7801.

Issues.Title: Stream resource downloads to disk instead of buffering them in memory
Issues.Body:
Fixes #5532

## Problem

`ResourceManagerUtils.DownloadResource` called `HttpClient.GetAsync` without an `HttpCompletionOption`, so the default `ResponseContentRead` buffered the whole response body in memory before returning.

For large resources such as `FastTextWikipedia300D` (`wiki.en.vec`, ~6.6 GB), `Content-Length` exceeds `HttpClient.MaxResponseContentBufferSize` (2 GB). The request fails immediately (before any bytes are transferred) with `Cannot write more bytes to the buffer than the configured maximum buffer size`, and each of the retries repeats the same failure. See the analysis and measurements in the issue thread.

## Changes

- Use `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead` and copy the response stream straight to the temp file, keeping memory use constant.
- Share a single `HttpClient` with an infinite per-request timeout; the existing outer timeout and the `CancellationToken` still bound the operation.
- Replace the thread-affine `Mutex` with a cross-process file lock. After an `await`, the continuation can run on a different thread than the one that acquired the `Mutex`, which makes `ReleaseMutex` throw.
- Dispose the `HttpResponseMessage`, drop the redundant second `EnsureSuccessStatusCode` call, and also handle `HttpRequestException` and `TaskCanceledException`.
- Make `DownloadResource` `internal` so it can be tested (`InternalsVisibleTo` for `Microsoft.ML.Core.Tests` already exists).

## Tests

Added offline loopback tests (`TestResourceDownloadBehavior`) covering:
- streaming the body to disk
- error HTTP status codes
- redirect to the default page
- cancellation

Added offline loopback tests (`TestResourceDownloadBehavior`) covering:
- streaming the body to disk
- error HTTP status codes
- redirect to the default page
- cancellation
- concurrent downloads of the same file

Local results: the 5 new tests and the existing `WordEmbeddings` tests pass on macOS arm64. I did not download the full 6.6 GB model in the test suite; a ~120 s sample against the live CDN is described in the issue.

Issues.Title: Fix broken aka.ms links and detect Bing fallback
Issues.Body:
An availability scan found three aka.ms links in active code/documentation that don't exist (anymore?):

- `https://aka.ms/MLNetIssue` — referenced by error/help messages in `src/Microsoft.ML.Data/Dirty/ModelParametersBase.cs`, `src/Microsoft.ML.Maml/MAML.cs`, and `src/Microsoft.ML.Transforms/Text/WordEmbeddingsExtractor.cs`.
- `https://aka.ms/mlnet` — referenced in 10 locations in historical release notes under `docs/release-notes/`.
- `https://aka.ms/mlnet-resources/datasets/flower_photos_small_set.zip` — referenced by three image-classification samples under `docs/samples/Microsoft.ML.Samples/Dynamic/Trainers/MulticlassClassification/ImageClassification/`.

The redirects return HTTP 200 after reaching Bing, so status-code-only link checks incorrectly report success. `src/Microsoft.ML.Core/Utilities/ResourceManagerUtils.cs` also detects only the older `https://www.microsoft.com/?ref=aka` fallback; if this helper is expected to identify invalid aka.ms links, update it to recognize the current Bing fallback and add regression coverage.

Please restore the intended aka.ms destinations where possible (or replace/remove stale historical links as appropriate), and consider adding a validation check that detects the fallback destination rather than relying on HTTP status.
